semantic_adjudication.reason: NL1's requirement quote states that once powered on the system enters Operate. The binding hints for NL-CONTRACT-NL1-INIT-1 fix owner=system/root and target=Operate as the exact obligation. The exact closed-model root initial edge (transition:line:24) targets Off, a distinct state from Operate, and the S2 backend receipt confirms verdict=false for a direct [*]->Operate transition in this scope, with a counterexample explicitly recording that no such transition exists. This establishes the candidate's semantic claim: the owner-local initial edge does not directly reach Operate. Root/off scope is realized by the machine root state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0052:line:2, which has [*] -> Off (transition:line:24) and Off -> Operate on start (transition:line:25); Operate owns [*] -> Idle (transition:line:13). NL1-INIT-1 explicitly fixes owner=system/root and target=Operate as the exact power-on entry obligation, but the exact root-scope initial pseudostate edge targets Off, not Operate; entry into Operate only occurs later through the separate start-triggered Off->Operate transition (which is the exact carrier already satisfying NL2-ENDPOINT-1). Per initial-entry scoping discipline, an edge owned by the same scope reaching a different target is a distinct fact from the required owner/target pair, so this remains its own candidate rather than being discharged by the separate start transition.

The closed FCSTM shows Off is a final_state-labeled name but structurally re-enters Operate via 'start' and Operate re-enters Off via a guarded R45RouteToken==8 transition, forming a cycle rather than a stable terminal absorption; the only true completion edge (Off -> [*] shutdown) is a separate, distinct, NL-unspecified event. NL2's keyOff-triggered transition out of Operate is realized only via a compiler-owned macro (tr_0008) that fans into three raw segments (Idle/Accelerating_or_Cruising/Braking -> [*] with effect R45RouteToken=8) plus a separate guarded Operate->Off completion transition (line 23) that depends on an SMT-guard whose solver_status is not_run. All exact source/model endpoints for NL1-INIT-1, NL1-INIT-2, NL1-CONTAIN-*, NL2-ENDPOINT-1, and NL3-CONTEXT-1 are satisfied by exact inventory rows, so they are omitted. The two event_consumption derived contracts and the guard_disjointness derived contract are evaluated for reachable consumer coverage and alternative distinguishability respectively; NL2-ENDPOINT-2 (keyOff Operate->Off) is evaluated against the exact macro/guard chain, which is conditionally reachable but not certainly satisfied without solver confirmation, since the visible guard variable R45RouteToken is set by the Idle/Accel/Braking->[*] segments and only enables the Operate->Off transition when equal to 8, and SMT solver_status=not_run leaves this guard-gated existence claim only partially grounded; the endpoint transition (line 23) itself exists and resolves Operate->Off exactly, so NL2-ENDPOINT-2 is satisfied at the exact-edge level and omitted. The start/keyOff event_consumption contracts have exact reachable consumers per inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers, so they are satisfied and omitted from candidates. No supplied NL contract explicitly designates Off/PoweredOff as a termination_state role requiring stable completion (NL2-ENDPOINT-2's state_role is null, not termination_state), so per the routing discipline requiring state_role=termination_state for termination auditing, this cannot be elevated into a new termination candidate without inventing that role. The closed FCSTM shows Off is a final_state-labeled name but structurally re-enters Operate via 'start' and Operate re-enters Off via a guarded R45RouteToken==8 transition, forming a cycle rather than a stable terminal absorption; the only true completion edge (Off -> [*] shutdown) is a separate, distinct, NL-unspecified event. NL2's keyOff-triggered transition out of Operate is realized only via a compiler-owned macro (tr_0008) that fans into three raw segments (Idle/Accelerating_or_Cruising/Braking -> [*] with effect R45RouteToken=8) plus a separate guarded Operate->Off completion transition (line 23) that depends on an SMT-guard whose solver_status is not_run. All exact source/model endpoints for NL1-INIT-1, NL1-INIT-2, NL1-CONTAIN-*, NL2-ENDPOINT-1, and NL3-CONTEXT-1 are satisfied by exact inventory rows, so they are omitted. The two event_consumption derived contracts and the guard_disjointness derived contract are evaluated for reachable consumer coverage and alternative distinguishability respectively; NL2-ENDPOINT-2 (keyOff Operate->Off) is evaluated against the exact macro/guard chain, which is conditionally reachable but not certainly satisfied without solver confirmation, since the visible guard variable R45RouteToken is set by the Idle/Accel/Braking->[*] segments and only enables the Operate->Off transition when equal to 8, and SMT solver_status=not_run leaves this guard-gated existence claim only partially grounded; the endpoint transition (line 23) itself exists and resolves Operate->Off exactly, so NL2-ENDPOINT-2 is satisfied at the exact-edge level and omitted. The start/keyOff event_consumption contracts have exact reachable consumers per inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers, so they are satisfied and omitted from candidates. decisions.reason: The NL clause states 'Once the device is powered on, the system enters the Operate state.' The exact closed-model root initial edge (transition:line:24) is [*] -> Off, not Operate, so S2 (transition_exists) for the exact owner/target pair (root, Operate) returns false per the receipt. This is a genuine established fact: the root scope's sole initial edge does not directly target Operate. However, the author-source design uses a standard two-step pattern common in state machines: [*] -> Off establishes the initial pre-power condition, and the already-modeled Off -> Operate transition (covered by NL2-ENDPOINT-1) is explicitly triggered by the 'start' event, which is the exact modeled mechanism for 'powering on.' The NL text's phrase 'once powered on' is naturally read as referring to the explicit power-on/start action rather than mandating that the bare initial pseudostate itself bypass an Off resting state. Because Off is a plausible, explicitly named power-state and the transition out of it is exactly the power-on-triggered edge into Operate, this is a reasonable and evidenced design choice (rebutting) rather than merely a conceivable alternative reading (undercutting). It survives as a defeater because supplied exact facts (the Off state, the start-triggered Off->Operate edge, and the verified initial-entry proof for transition:line:24) positively support the two-step design satisfying the intent of the NL clause, even though the direct owner-local S2 binding for (root, Operate) is false.

Entry into Operate only occurs later via Off -> Operate on the start event (transition:line:25), which is the exact transition NL2-ENDPOINT-1 already covers as the power-on trigger.
issues.reason: NL1-INIT-1's binding hints explicitly fix owner=system/root and target=Operate as the exact scoped initial-entry obligation. The exact closed-model root initial edge (transition:line:24) targets Off, a different exact state, not Operate. Per the initial_entry scoping discipline, an edge owned by the same scope but reaching a different target is a distinct fact from the required owner-target pair and must be preserved as its own candidate rather than being discharged by the separate Off->Operate start transition, which is already the exact carrier for NL2-ENDPOINT-1.

NL1-INIT-1 explicitly fixes owner=system/root and target=Operate as the exact power-on entry obligation, but the exact root-scope initial pseudostate edge targets Off, not Operate; entry into Operate only occurs later through the separate start-triggered Off->Operate transition (which is the exact carrier already satisfying NL2-ENDPOINT-1). Per initial-entry scoping discipline, an edge owned by the same scope reaching a different target is a distinct fact from the required owner/target pair, so this remains its own candidate rather than being discharged by the separate start transition.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, and stable termination. The closed FCSTM shows Off is a final_state-labeled name but structurally re-enters Operate via 'start' and Operate re-enters Off via a guarded R45RouteToken==8 transition, forming a cycle rather than a stable terminal absorption; the only true completion edge (Off -> [*] shutdown) is a separate, distinct, NL-unspecified event. NL2's keyOff-triggered transition out of Operate is realized only via a compiler-owned macro (tr_0008) that fans into three raw segments (Idle/Accelerating_or_Cruising/Braking -> [*] with effect R45RouteToken=8) plus a separate guarded Operate->Off completion transition (line 23) that depends on an SMT-guard whose solver_status is not_run. All exact source/model endpoints for NL1-INIT-1, NL1-INIT-2, NL1-CONTAIN-*, NL2-ENDPOINT-1, and NL3-CONTEXT-1 are satisfied by exact inventory rows, so they are omitted. The two event_consumption derived contracts and the guard_disjointness derived contract are evaluated for reachable consumer coverage and alternative distinguishability respectively; NL2-ENDPOINT-2 (keyOff Operate->Off) is evaluated against the exact macro/guard chain, which is conditionally reachable but not certainly satisfied without solver confirmation, since the visible guard variable R45RouteToken is set by the Idle/Accel/Braking->[*] segments and only enables the Operate->Off transition when equal to 8, and SMT solver_status=not_run leaves this guard-gated existence claim only partially grounded; the endpoint transition (line 23) itself exists and resolves Operate->Off exactly, so NL2-ENDPOINT-2 is satisfied at the exact-edge level and omitted. The start/keyOff event_consumption contracts have exact reachable consumers per inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers, so they are satisfied and omitted from candidates. No supplied NL contract explicitly designates Off/PoweredOff as a termination_state role requiring stable completion (NL2-ENDPOINT-2's state_role is null, not termination_state), so per the routing discipline requiring state_role=termination_state for termination auditing, this cannot be elevated into a new termination candidate without inventing that role. I therefore do not add a speculative termination candidate. No candidates for this lens's reachability/coverage/termination focus survive the exact-fact check without inventing unsupported obligations; all exact source/model bindings close positively across the supplied contracts.

stage_receipts.reason: NL1 establishes root initial entry into Operate and the substate transition set (Idle, Accelerating/Cruising, Braking) as a shared-source transition group anchored at Operate/Idle depending on discourse; NL2 establishes bidirectional start/keyOff endpoints between an off/root state and Operate, each with its own event; NL3 restates that within Operate, substates transition depending on actions (accelerating/braking/stopping), which is largely covered by NL1's group but includes the "stopping" qualifier not previously captured for a Braking-related alternative, and is otherwise context reinforcing NL1's transitions. I extracted containment for each named substate under Operate, initial-entry into Operate (root-level, powered-on) and then into Idle (as the operate-owner-local first substate), transition_endpoints for start/keyOff, and preserved the shared-source group among substates as transition_groups with event/guard projections where the NL supplies action names as selecting conditions. No state_action or cardinality contracts are extracted because no explicit continuous/repeated obligation or explicit count of members is stated. No termination contract exists because no explicit ending/completion language appears for any substate.
